description: What an audit of examples/neem-square should find and what it should leave alone. Follow examples/neem-square.run-sheet.md: a cold session copies the app outside the repo, runs /classify and /audit and never opens this file; a separate session scores the result. Each file is where the gap is easiest to anchor; the issue text names the other files needed to work it out. Clauses are the expected anchors, all IT-RULES, written as catalog/rules.json writes them. One finding that covers two planted items counts for both. fair_if_reported lists absences a careful audit may report at medium or lower: they count neither as hits nor as false positives.

classification.why: Users post and share content with each other; the README gives about 62 lakh registered users in India, over the 50 lakh threshold; Imagine generates and edits images. Neem Square sells nothing, so no ecom tag.

expected.issue: The grievance page gives a role mailbox and a form but names no Grievance Officer. web/templates/contact.html names the Chief Compliance Officer and the nodal contact person, and no Resident Grievance Officer anywhere.

The grievance page is not on the home page or directly reachable from it. web/templates/home.html includes the footer, which has no grievance link; the path is Home, Help, Legal and safety, Grievance redressal (web/routes.py: /help/legal/grievance).
The only postal address published is the Singapore parent's, and legal notices are directed there. No physical contact address in India.
resolve_days is 15, which services/grievance/intake.py applies as the due date for ordinary complaints. The rule gives 7 days.
content_removal_hours is 72, applied by due_at() in services/grievance/intake.py to content_removal and synthetic_media reports. The rule gives 36 hours for removal complaints.
NCII_SLA is 24 hours and the queue pages a second time only after 12 hours, for intimate imagery and impersonation or morphed image reports. The rule gives 2 hours.

The runbook targets removal within 36 hours and leaves orders that arrive out of hours to the next working day. config/oncall.yaml staffs legal-orders on weekdays 10:00 to 18:00 by email, and posted orders go to Singapore and are scanned weekly. None of that can meet 3 hours.
KEEP_REMOVED is 30 days. The job deletes removed posts with their media, comments and moderation_events, which are the associated records. The rule requires 180 days.

GRACE is 30 days. The job deletes signup_records (email, phone, date of birth, signup IP and time) and the user row 30 days after closure, as web/legal/privacy.md promises. The rule requires registration information to be retained for 180 days. The finding should name the DPDP erasure tension and point to Vigil without resolving it.
terms_reminder runs on cron '0 9 15 1 *': once a year, on 15 January, though the comment calls it periodic. The rule requires at least once every three months.

The reminder text carries only the first limb: removal, suspension or closure. It does not say the user may face penalty or punishment under law, or that offences which must be reported will be reported.

Section 3 on Imagine says to use it responsibly and not to mislead. It does not warn that unlawful synthetic content may attract penalty or punishment under the listed laws, or set out the consequences: removal, account suspension, identity disclosure to a victim, mandatory reporting. web/legal/community-guidelines.md and jobs/terms_reminder.py do not either.

image_to_image() calls neither safety.check_prompt nor safety.check_output, while text_to_image() calls both. The edit path takes an uploaded photo of a real person and an instruction to change what they are wearing or doing, with no filter.

prepare_for_feed() drops EXIF, XMP and IPTC from every post. api/posts.py sends Imagine assets through it, so the provenance fields that services/imagine/provenance.py wrote, including the unique asset id, are gone from the published image.
creators.clean_export is true, and _finish() in services/imagine/generate.py skips the burned-in label for verified creators. The platform itself enables removal of the label.

The post form has no declaration of whether the content is synthetically generated, api/posts.py stores none and runs no check on uploads, and nothing renders a label from a declaration or a detection. An SSMI must do all three before publication.
remove_for_policy() removes content on the platform's own enforcement with no notice to the uploader and no route to dispute it or ask for reinstatement. Only remove_for_copyright() notifies.

should_not_flag.why: ack_hours is 24, which is the acknowledgement period. Only resolve_days and content_removal_hours are stale.

create() sends the acknowledgement automatically, issues a unique ticket number and status() backs a public status page, so neither a missing acknowledgement nor a missing ticket number under Rule 4(6) may be reported.

Section 2 covers sub-clauses (i) to (viii) and (xi) of Rule 3(1)(b) in substance; (ix) and (x) concern online games and the product has none. The three documents exist and the footer on the home page links each. Section 3 is a different matter (P12).
The 72-hour clock matches Rule 3(1)(j), the request must be a written order stating its purpose, and the lea-liaison rota is staffed at all hours.

The Chief Compliance Officer and the nodal contact person are named, are different people, and are stated to be based in India. Only the Resident Grievance Officer (P1) and the India address (P3) are missing.
The report runs on the first of every month (config/schedules.yaml), carries complaints received, action taken and proactive removals, and is published at /transparency.

At generation the image gets a burned-in label and XMP provenance with a unique asset id. The generator must not be reported as writing no label or no metadata; the gaps are what happens afterwards (P14) and the creator exemption (P15).

The text-to-image path checks the prompt and the output against the listed topics and fails closed when the classifier is down. It must not be reported that Imagine has no technical measures; the gap is the edit path (P13).
The Merch link opens a third party's shop and the README says Neem Square sells nothing. No ECOM-RULES finding is correct.
The closure message gives reasons and tells the complainant about the Grievance Appellate Committee and the 30-day window.

The report form has categories for intimate imagery and for impersonation or morphed images, takes reports from non-users and on behalf of someone else, so the Rule 3(2)(c) mechanism exists. The gap is the clock (P6).
disable_content() is an admin action by content id that needs no deploy and writes an audit log, so a missing takedown action or audit log may not be reported. remove_for_policy is P17.
Synthetic complaints. No finding should rest on them, and no name, email or complaint text from them may appear in any output.

fair_if_reported: No step for complying with a Grievance Appellate Committee order or posting the compliance report (Rule 3A(7)): not found in the reviewed material.
No hash matching or review record for proactive detection (Rule 4(4)); jobs/compliance_report.py counts 'policy:auto' removals, so some automated tool exists.
The Terms promise notice of changes but no job or template sends one (Rule 3(1)(f)).
docs/runbooks/legal-orders.md names counsel, not the Grievance Officer, as the recipient of orders (Rule 3(2)(a)(ii)), and was last reviewed in August 2025.
Nothing renders an AI label in the feed from posts.source; the label exists only as burned-in pixels (Rule 4(1A)(c), Rule 3(3)(a)(ii)).
synthetic_media reports have a queue but no playbook for account action or identity disclosure (Rule 3(1)(cb)).
web/templates/grievance.html states no resolution period and does not give the appeal window (Rule 3A(3), good practice only).
